Privacy Guarantee: 100% Client-Side. Financial records, budgets, and transactions are stored exclusively in the user's browser memory (IndexedDB and localStorage). Zero server databases, zero bank login aggregators.

1. ARCHITECTURE, AUTHOR & PRIVACY MODEL
================================================================================
Author: Prince Upadhyay
Background: Prince Upadhyay is a CA (Chartered Accountancy) Intermediate student based in India. He created FreeExpenseTracker.com to counter the aggressive monetization of modern budgeting apps, which charge recurring subscriptions, force users to link sensitive banking credentials through third-party data aggregators, and sell user financial habits to advertisers.
Mission: Democratizing access to transparent, privacy-first personal financial management tools with zero cost, zero friction, and zero sign-up hurdles.
Privacy Architecture:
- Local Storage & IndexedDB: All transaction records, expense ledgers, debt balances, and target goals are stored exclusively inside the client's browser database (FreeExpenseTrackerDB in IndexedDB with localStorage fallback).
- In-Browser OCR & File Parsing: Uploaded receipts and PDF/CSV/XLSX bank statements are processed entirely in memory via client-side WebAssembly and Web Workers (tesseract.js and pdfjs-dist). Files are never transmitted over the internet to any external server.
- Analytics: Standard privacy-compliant Google Analytics 4 (Measurement ID: G-XR6MG2FM4M) collects anonymous traffic metrics. No financial data, transaction details, or monetary numbers are ever sent to analytics.

2. LIVE INTERACTIVE EXPENSE TRACKER (HOMEPAGE)
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/
Title: Free Expense Tracker - Private, Fast & In-Browser Personal Finance Tracker

Introductory Answer:
FreeExpenseTracker is a 100% free, client-side personal finance web application for individuals and households seeking private expense tracking. It solves budgeting complexity and privacy concerns by calculating real-time cash flow, category breakdowns, and financial health scores entirely inside your browser, requiring zero sign-up, no bank passwords, and no subscriptions.

How It Works & Calculation Methodology:
The live expense tracker calculates net monthly cash flow and evaluates spending against the 50/30/20 budgeting rule (Needs 50%, Wants 30%, Savings 20%).
Formulas:
- Net Cash Flow = Total Normalized Monthly Income - Total Monthly Outflows
- Savings Rate (%) = (Total Savings Allocated ÷ Total Normalized Monthly Income) × 100
- Outflow Ratio (%) = (Total Monthly Outflows ÷ Total Normalized Monthly Income) × 100
- Financial Health Score = Weighted composite metric benchmarking Savings Rate (target >= 20%), Fixed Cost Ratio (target <= 50%), and Emergency Runway.

Numerical Worked Example:
- Normalized Monthly Income: $5,000.00
- Monthly Outflows: Housing $1,800 + Food $600 + Utilities $300 + Transport $400 + Entertainment $400 = $3,500.00
- Monthly Savings Allocated: $1,500.00
- Calculations:
  - Net Cash Flow: $5,000.00 - $3,500.00 = +$1,500.00
  - Outflow Ratio: ($3,500 ÷ $5,000) × 100 = 70%
  - Savings Rate: ($1,500 ÷ $5,000) × 100 = 30% (Exceeds the 20% benchmark, resulting in an "Excellent" health indicator).

Frequently Asked Questions:
Q: Is FreeExpenseTracker free?
A: Yes, FreeExpenseTracker is 100% free with no paid subscriptions, premium tiers, or hidden fees. All budgeting tools, calculators, and spreadsheet downloads are unlocked for everyone with zero advertisements.
Q: Do I need to create an account?
A: No account registration or sign-up is required. You can start logging expenses, modeling debt payoffs, and downloading spreadsheet templates immediately upon opening the website.
Q: Is my financial information stored online?
A: No, your financial information is never transmitted to or stored on external servers. All transaction ledgers, income figures, and calculations remain exclusively on your device inside your browser's private local storage and IndexedDB.

3. MULTI-CURRENCY BILL SPLITTER CALCULATOR
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/bill-splitter/
Title: Free Bill Splitter Calculator (No Sign-Up)

Introductory Answer:
FreeExpenseTracker Bill Splitter is a free, browser-based group expense calculator designed for roommates, diners, and travel groups. It solves awkward bill-splitting disputes by calculating equal splits, proportional tax and tip allocations for itemized meals, and multi-person debt settlement with minimal cash transfers—completely free, private, and requiring no account registration.

How It Works & Calculation Methodology:
The Bill Splitter provides three distinct splitting modes:
1. Equal Split Mode: Divides the total bill (including tax and tip) evenly among N participants.
   Formula: Each Person's Share = (Subtotal + Tax + Tip) ÷ Number of People
2. Itemized Split Mode (Proportional Tax & Tip):
   Each participant pays for their specific consumed items. Shared tax and tips are distributed proportionally using the Largest Remainder Method (Hare-Niemeyer method) to ensure fair distribution and exact currency minor-unit precision.
   Formula: Person's Share = Item Subtotal + (Item Subtotal ÷ Food Subtotal) × Total Tax + (Item Subtotal ÷ Food Subtotal) × Total Tip
3. Trip / Group Split Mode (Debt Simplification):
   Calculates each participant's net balance: Net Balance = Total Money Paid - Total Fair Share Owed.
   A greedy minimum-cash-flow algorithm iteratively matches the largest debtor with the largest creditor until all balances are settled in at most N-1 transactions.

Numerical Worked Examples:
- Equal Split Example:
  A ₹1,500 restaurant bill divided equally among 3 friends:
  ₹1,500 ÷ 3 = ₹500 per person.
- Itemized Split Example:
  Food Subtotal = ₹1,000 (Person A ordered ₹600, Person B ordered ₹400). Tip = ₹100 (10%).
  - Person A's Share: ₹600 + (₹600 ÷ ₹1,000) × ₹100 = ₹600 + ₹60 = ₹660.
  - Person B's Share: ₹400 + (₹400 ÷ ₹1,000) × ₹100 = ₹400 + ₹40 = ₹440.
  - Total Verified: ₹660 + ₹440 = ₹1,100.
- Debt Simplification Example:
  Three roommates: Alice paid ₹3,000 for groceries, Bob paid ₹1,500 for utilities, Charlie paid ₹0. Total = ₹4,500. Fair share per person = ₹1,500.
  - Alice Net Balance: ₹3,000 - ₹1,500 = +₹1,500 (Creditor)
  - Bob Net Balance: ₹1,500 - ₹1,500 = ₹0 (Settled)
  - Charlie Net Balance: ₹0 - ₹1,500 = -₹1,500 (Debtor)
  - Result: Charlie pays Alice ₹1,500 directly in exactly 1 transfer.

Frequently Asked Questions:
Q: How do I split a bill with different amounts?
A: Use the Itemized Split mode in our Bill Splitter to assign dishes, drinks, or items to specific people with their exact prices. The tool automatically computes individual subtotals and proportionally allocates shared taxes and tips based on each person's consumption.
Q: How does the bill splitter handle taxes and tips for shared items?
A: Taxes and tips are distributed proportionally based on each person's consumed subtotal using the Largest Remainder Method. This ensures someone ordering an inexpensive side dish does not pay an unfair share of tax and tips.
Q: Which currencies are supported?
A: 10 major global currencies are supported: INR (₹), USD ($), EUR (€), GBP (£), CAD ($), AUD ($), SGD ($), AED (AED), CHF (CHF), and JPY (¥). Zero-decimal currencies like JPY are automatically rounded to whole numbers.

4. DEBT SNOWBALL SPREADSHEET CALCULATOR
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/debt-snowball/
Title: Free Debt Snowball Spreadsheet (Excel & Google Sheets)

Introductory Answer:
The Free Debt Snowball Spreadsheet is a downloadable Excel and Google Sheets workbook for individuals looking to eliminate multiple consumer debts using behavioral psychology. It solves debt payoff burnout by prioritizing the smallest balances first to generate fast motivational wins, completely free and requiring no email sign-up.

How It Works & Calculation Methodology:
The Debt Snowball strategy orders all debts by current outstanding principal balance in ascending order (smallest balance first), regardless of interest rates.
Methodology:
1. Pay mandatory minimum monthly payments on all debts to remain in good standing.
2. Direct all available extra debt prepayment funds toward Debt #1 (smallest balance).
3. Once Debt #1 reaches zero, roll its entire monthly budget (minimum payment + extra payment) into Debt #2.
4. Repeat this expanding snowball effect until all debts are paid off.

Numerical Worked Example:
Three consumer debts:
- Debt A (Medical Bill): Balance = ₹5,000, APR = 12%, Minimum Payment = ₹250/mo.
- Debt B (Credit Card): Balance = ₹15,000, APR = 18%, Minimum Payment = ₹500/mo.
- Debt C (Personal Loan): Balance = ₹30,000, APR = 9%, Minimum Payment = ₹800/mo.
Extra Prepayment Budget Available = ₹1,000/mo.
Action Plan:
- Prioritize Debt A (₹5,000 balance). Pay ₹250 (minimum) + ₹1,000 (extra) = ₹1,250/month.
- Pay minimums on Debt B (₹500) and Debt C (₹800).
- Debt A is eliminated in approximately 4 months.
- Its entire ₹1,250 budget then rolls into Debt B, raising Debt B's monthly payment to ₹500 + ₹1,250 = ₹1,750/month, knocking out the ₹15,000 card rapidly.

Frequently Asked Questions:
Q: How does the debt snowball method work?
A: The debt snowball method prioritizes paying off your smallest balance first while maintaining minimum payments on all other accounts. Once the smallest debt reaches zero, its entire monthly payment rolls into the next smallest balance, building psychological momentum to eliminate debt faster.
Q: What is the difference between debt snowball and avalanche?
A: The debt snowball targets the smallest balance first for psychological motivation, while the debt avalanche targets the highest interest rate (APR) first for mathematical interest savings. Both methods significantly outperform paying only minimums.

5. DEBT AVALANCHE SPREADSHEET CALCULATOR
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/debt-avalanche/
Title: Free Debt Avalanche Calculator Spreadsheet (.xlsx)

Introductory Answer:
The Free Debt Avalanche Spreadsheet is an Excel and Google Sheets financial calculator designed for borrowers focused on minimizing lifetime interest expenses. It solves high interest costs by mathematically prioritizing the debt with the highest annual percentage rate (APR) first, free to download with zero registration.

How It Works & Calculation Methodology:
The Debt Avalanche strategy orders all debts by Annual Percentage Rate (APR) in descending order (highest interest rate first).
Methodology:
1. Pay mandatory minimum payments on all accounts.
2. Direct all extra monthly payments to the debt charging the highest APR.
3. When the highest-rate debt is cleared, roll its entire payment into the next highest APR balance.

Numerical Worked Example:
Three debts:
- Debt A: ₹5,000 balance at 12% APR (Minimum: ₹250/mo)
- Debt B: ₹15,000 balance at 18% APR (Minimum: ₹500/mo)
- Debt C: ₹30,000 balance at 9% APR (Minimum: ₹800/mo)
Extra Monthly Debt Budget = ₹1,000/mo.
Action Plan:
- Under Debt Avalanche, prioritize Debt B first because its 18% APR is the highest interest rate.
- Monthly payment on Debt B = ₹500 (minimum) + ₹1,000 (extra) = ₹1,500/month.
- Pay minimums on Debt A (₹250) and Debt C (₹800).
- Targeting the 18% loan first prevents high compounding interest and saves the maximum amount of money over the life of the debts.

6. DEBT-TO-INCOME (DTI) RATIO PLANNER
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/debt-to-income-calculator/
Title: Free Debt-to-Income (DTI) Calculator Spreadsheet

Introductory Answer:
The Free Debt-to-Income Ratio Planner is a downloadable spreadsheet tool for prospective homebuyers and borrowers assessing their credit readiness. It solves mortgage qualification uncertainty by calculating front-end housing and back-end total debt-to-income percentages against standard lending thresholds, completely free with no registration.

How It Works & Calculation Methodology:
Lenders evaluate two DTI ratios:
1. Front-End DTI (Housing Ratio):
   Formula: Front-End DTI = (Monthly Housing Costs ÷ Gross Monthly Income) × 100
   Benchmark: Ideally 28% or lower.
2. Back-End DTI (Total Debt Ratio):
   Formula: Back-End DTI = (Total Monthly Debt Payments ÷ Gross Monthly Income) × 100
   Total Monthly Debt includes: mortgage/rent, student loans, auto loans, minimum credit card payments, and personal loans.
   Benchmark: Under 36% is considered healthy; 43% is generally the maximum limit for conventional mortgages.

Numerical Worked Example:
- Gross Monthly Income: ₹60,000.00
- Monthly Debt Obligations:
  - Auto Loan EMI: ₹8,000
  - Credit Card Minimums: ₹3,000
  - Personal Loan: ₹4,000
  - Total Monthly Debt Payments: ₹15,000.00
- Calculation:
  DTI = (₹15,000 ÷ ₹60,000) × 100 = 25.0%
- Assessment: A 25% DTI is well below the standard 36% maximum benchmark, representing strong borrowing health and high loan approval probability.

Frequently Asked Questions:
Q: How do I calculate my debt-to-income ratio?
A: To calculate your debt-to-income (DTI) ratio, divide your total monthly debt payments by your gross monthly income and multiply by 100. For example, ₹15,000 in monthly debt divided by ₹60,000 gross monthly income equals a 25% DTI, which is considered financially healthy.

7. PAYCHECK BUDGET SPREADSHEET
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/paycheck-budget/
Title: Free Paycheck Budget Spreadsheet (Excel .xlsx)

Introductory Answer:
The Free Paycheck Budget Spreadsheet is a zero-based cash flow template designed for biweekly, weekly, or semi-monthly earners. It solves the timing mismatch between bill due dates and paycheck deposits by allocating every dollar of take-home pay before spending occurs, free to download without signing up.

How It Works & Formulas:
Formula: Remaining Unallocated Cash = Net Paycheck Income - (Fixed Bills + Variable Allowances + Sinking Funds + Debt Payments).
The goal is to reach zero unallocated dollars, ensuring every unit of currency is deliberately assigned.
Worked Example:
- Net Biweekly Paycheck: $2,400.00
- Fixed Bills (Due this pay cycle): Rent $900 + Electric $120 + Phone $80 = $1,100
- Variable Spending: Groceries $350 + Gas $100 + Dining $150 = $600
- Savings Allocation: Emergency fund $400
- Debt Principal Prepayment: $300
- Remaining Cash = $2,400 - ($1,100 + $600 + $400 + $300) = $0.00 (Zero-based balance achieved).

8. STUDENT LOAN PAYOFF PLANNER
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/student-loan-planner/
Title: Free Student Loan Payoff Planner Spreadsheet (.xlsx)

Introductory Answer:
The Free Student Loan Payoff Planner is an amortization workbook for graduates tackling higher education debt. It solves repayment ambiguity by modeling extra monthly principal payments, comparing standard versus accelerated timelines, and computing total interest saved, 100% free with no sign-up required.

Formula:
Monthly Payment (PMT) = P × [r(1 + r)^n] ÷ [(1 + r)^n - 1]
where P = principal loan balance, r = monthly interest rate (APR ÷ 12), n = total number of months.
Worked Example:
- Student Loan Balance: $35,000 at 6.0% APR (10-year standard term).
- Standard Monthly Payment: $388.57. Total Interest Paid = $11,629 over 120 months.
- Extra Monthly Payment: +$150/month (Total = $538.57/month).
- New Payoff Time: 80 months (6.6 years, saving 3.4 years).
- Total Interest Paid: $7,632 (Net savings of $3,997 in interest).

9. AUTO LOAN CALCULATOR
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/auto-loan-calculator/
Title: Free Auto Loan Calculator Spreadsheet (.xlsx)

Introductory Answer:
The Free Auto Loan Calculator is an amortization spreadsheet for vehicle buyers evaluating financing options. It solves car dealership financing confusion by calculating exact monthly payments, loan interest, sales tax, and dealer fees, completely free and requiring no email registration.

Formula:
Loan Amount = Vehicle Purchase Price - Down Payment - Trade-in Value + Taxes & Fees.
Monthly Payment = Loan Amount × [r(1 + r)^n] ÷ [(1 + r)^n - 1]
Worked Example:
- Vehicle Price: $28,000. Down Payment: $5,000. Net Financed: $23,000.
- Term: 60 months (5 years) at 5.5% APR.
- Monthly Payment = $439.43. Total Interest = $3,365.80. Total Cost = $26,365.80.

Accelerated Amortization: Principal Reduction per Month = Regular Scheduled Principal + Extra Prepayment.

11. 401(K) RETIREMENT FORECASTER
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/401k-retirement-planner/
Title: Free 401(k) Retirement Calculator Spreadsheet

Introductory Answer:
The Free 401(k) Retirement Forecaster is a long-term investment projection workbook for working professionals planning retirement. It solves retirement planning guesswork by modeling employer matching, annual salary increases, and compound growth, free to download with zero registration.

Formula:
Future Value = PV × (1 + r)^t + PMT × [((1 + r)^t - 1) ÷ r]
Worked Example:
- Current 401(k) Balance: $25,000. Annual Salary: $80,000.
- Employee Contribution: 6% ($4,800/yr). Employer Match: 3% ($2,400/yr). Total Annual Contribution = $7,200 ($600/mo).
- Expected Annual Return: 7.0% over 30 years.
- Projected Nest Egg at Age 65: $775,800.

================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/emergency-fund-planner/
Title: Free Emergency Fund Planner (.xlsx)

Introductory Answer:
The Free Emergency Fund Planner is a cash cushion calculation spreadsheet for individuals building a financial safety net. It solves unexpected financial emergency stress by computing 3, 6, and 9-month essential living expense targets and monthly funding timelines, free with zero sign-up.

Formula:
Target Emergency Reserve = Essential Baseline Monthly Living Expenses × Target Months (3, 6, or 9).
Worked Example:
- Essential Monthly Needs: Rent $1,500 + Food $500 + Utilities $250 + Insurance $200 + Minimum Debt Payments $350 = $2,800/month.
- 3-Month Starter Safety Net: $2,800 × 3 = $8,400.
- 6-Month Full Emergency Fund: $2,800 × 6 = $16,800.
- Saving $400/month funds the 3-month reserve in 21 months.

The Free Subscription Audit Worksheet is a recurring expense management workbook for budgeters eliminating subscription creep. It solves forgotten recurring charges by cataloging streaming, cloud, and app subscriptions, converting billing frequencies to annual totals, 100% free with no sign-up.

Formula:
Annualized Subscription Cost = (Monthly Rate × 12) or (Weekly Rate × 52) or (Quarterly Rate × 4).
Worked Example:
- Netflix ($15.49/mo) = $185.88/yr
- Spotify ($11.99/mo) = $143.88/yr

15. SINKING FUND PLANNER
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/sinking-fund-planner/
Title: Free Sinking Fund Planner Spreadsheet (.xlsx)

Introductory Answer:
The Free Sinking Fund Planner is an irregular expense budgeting workbook for proactive financial planners. It solves budget-busting periodic bills by dividing future expected costs into predictable monthly savings deposits, completely free with no sign-up needed.

Formula:
Monthly Contribution = (Target Future Cost - Current Amount Saved) ÷ Months Until Due.
Worked Example:
- Auto Insurance: $1,200 due in 6 months. Current saved = $0. Monthly Contribution = $1,200 ÷ 6 = $200/month.
- Holiday Gifts: $600 due in 10 months. Current saved = $100. Monthly Contribution = ($600 - $100) ÷ 10 = $50/month.

16. NET WORTH TRACKER
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/net-worth-tracker/
Title: Free Net Worth Tracker Spreadsheet (.xlsx)

Introductory Answer:
The Free Net Worth Tracker is a personal balance sheet spreadsheet for wealth builders monitoring their financial trajectory. It solves holistic wealth tracking by aggregating cash, investments, and property against liabilities to compute true net worth over time, 100% free with zero sign-up.

Formula:
Net Worth = Total Assets (Cash + Investments + Real Estate + Retirement) - Total Liabilities (Mortgages + Auto Loans + Credit Cards + Student Loans).
Worked Example:
- Assets: Checking $4,000 + Emergency Fund $15,000 + 401(k) $65,000 + Car Market Value $18,000 = $102,000.
- Liabilities: Auto Loan $11,000 + Credit Card Balance $2,000 + Student Loans $24,000 = $37,000.
- Net Worth = $102,000 - $37,000 = +$65,000.

20. 52-WEEK SAVINGS CHALLENGE ($1,378)
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/52-week-savings-challenge/
Title: Free 52-Week Savings Challenge Spreadsheet (.xlsx & Google Sheets)

Introductory Answer:
The Free 52-Week Savings Challenge Spreadsheet is an automated incremental savings ladder for individuals building a savings habit. It solves saving inconsistency by guiding you to save $1 in Week 1, $2 in Week 2, through $52 in Week 52, accumulating $1,378 in one year with no sign-up needed.

Formula:
Total Saved = n(n + 1) ÷ 2 where n = 52 weeks.
Total Accumulated = 52 × 53 ÷ 2 = $1,378.00.
Worked Example:
- Week 1: Save $1 (Cumulative: $1)
- Week 10: Save $10 (Cumulative: $55)
- Week 26 (Halfway): Save $26 (Cumulative: $351)
- Week 52: Save $52 (Cumulative: $1,378.00).

23. BIWEEKLY SAVINGS CHALLENGE ($1,378 / 26 PAYCHECKS)
================================================================================
URL: https://freexpensetracker.com/templates/biweekly-savings-challenge/
Title: Free Biweekly Savings Challenge Spreadsheet (.xlsx)

Introductory Answer:
The Free Biweekly Savings Challenge Spreadsheet is a paycheck-aligned savings ladder for workers paid every two weeks. It solves calendar mismatch by distributing the classic $1,378 annual goal across 26 paychecks with progressive deposits, 100% free with no sign-up required.

Formula:
Deposit for Paycheck k (1 to 26) = (2k - 1) + 2k = 4k - 1.
Total Accumulated over 26 paychecks = $1,378.00.
Worked Example:
- Paycheck 1: $1 + $2 = $3
- Paycheck 2: $3 + $4 = $7
- Paycheck 13 (Midpoint): $25 + $26 = $51 (Cumulative: $351)
- Paycheck 26: $51 + $52 = $103 (Cumulative: $1,378.00).

25. UNIVERSAL FREQUENTLY ASKED QUESTIONS (FAQ)
================================================================================
Q1: Is FreeExpenseTracker free?
A1: Yes, FreeExpenseTracker is 100% free with no paid subscriptions, premium tiers, or hidden fees. All budgeting tools, calculators, and spreadsheet downloads are unlocked for everyone with zero advertisements.

Q2: Do I need to create an account?
A2: No account registration or sign-up is required. You can start logging expenses, modeling debt payoffs, and downloading spreadsheet templates immediately upon opening the website.

Q3: Is my financial information stored online?
A3: No, your financial information is never transmitted to or stored on external servers. All transaction ledgers, income figures, and calculations remain exclusively on your device inside your browser's private local storage and IndexedDB.

Q4: How do I make my own expense tracker?
A4: To make your own expense tracker, set up columns for Date, Description, Category, Payment Method, and Outflow Amount in a spreadsheet or physical ledger. Alternatively, you can use FreeExpenseTracker's pre-configured live dashboard or free downloadable Excel workbooks to begin tracking immediately.

Q5: How does the debt snowball method work?
A5: The debt snowball method prioritizes paying off your smallest balance first while maintaining minimum payments on all other accounts. Once the smallest debt reaches zero, its entire monthly payment rolls into the next smallest balance, building psychological momentum to eliminate debt faster.

Q6: What is the difference between debt snowball and avalanche?
A6: The debt snowball method targets the smallest loan balance first to build early motivational wins, whereas the debt avalanche method attacks the debt with the highest interest rate (APR) first to minimize total interest paid. Both strategies accelerate debt elimination compared to making only minimum payments.

Q7: How do I calculate my debt-to-income ratio?
A7: To calculate your debt-to-income (DTI) ratio, divide your total monthly debt payments by your gross monthly income and multiply by 100. For example, ₹15,000 in monthly debt divided by ₹60,000 gross monthly income equals a 25% DTI, which is considered financially healthy.

Q8: How do I split a bill with different amounts?
A8: Use the Itemized Split mode in our Bill Splitter to assign dishes, drinks, or items to specific people with their exact prices. The tool automatically computes individual subtotals and proportionally allocates shared taxes and tips based on each person's consumption.
